hypotheses.title: Analyst Coverage Breadth Expansion and Institutional Discovery Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Sell-side analyst attention is an institutional scarce resource. When the number of equity research analysts providing annual EPS forecasts (anl4_afv4_eps_number, Matrix 100% coverage) expands relative to its rolling standard deviation, it reflects institutional discovery, enhanced corporate transparency, and reduced information asymmetry. Under Merton's (1987) investor recognition hypothesis, expanding analyst coverage lowers the equity cost of capital and produces persistent forward price appreciation.
confounders: Sudden corporate controversies or short seller reports that attract analyst downgrades and negative scrutiny
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if analyst coverage expansion yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 10-day decay of 20-day change in analyst coverage count normalized by trailing 60-day coverage volatility.

hypotheses.title: Actual Operating Cash Flow Yield Accretion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Actual Cash Flow Per Share (anl4_af_cfps_value, Matrix 100% permitted) measures organic liquidity generation per share devoid of non-cash accounting accruals. Scaling cash flow per share by the equity price provides a pristine cash yield metric. Firms generating high organic cash yields relative to subindustry peers trade at an unwarranted valuation discount that unwinds as cash accumulation forces dividend increases or share repurchases.
confounders: Cyclical capital goods industries where working capital swings temporarily inflate annual cash flow per share
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cash flow per share yield yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 10-day decay of actual cash flow per share scaled by closing stock price.

hypotheses.title: Supply-Chain Clustered Idiosyncratic Risk Premia Harvest
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Elevated unsystematic variance (unsystematic_risk_last_90_days, 96% coverage) reflects temporary firm-specific operational or headline uncertainty that causes retail panic selling. By neutralizing and ranking the negative of 90-day unsystematic risk within granular supply-chain network clusters (pv13_h_min2_3000_sector, Group 100% coverage in TOP3000), we isolate genuine calm, idiosyncratic resilience while eliminating common production network and supply-chain factor noise.
confounders: Major structural macroeconomic regime shifts that disrupt supply chain hierarchies across all peer tiers simultaneously
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if supply-chain clustered idiosyncratic risk normalization yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Negative 10-day decay of 90-day unsystematic risk ranked within supply-chain network sector clusters.
